contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: batch operations are applied sequentially in the order given; each operation reports its own result
contract_grounding.note: Dispatch constraint_id was empty; the script header pins two co-anchors (qdrant_behavioral_points_batch_001 + qdrant_state_points_batch_001) and the E1 oracle tests end-state application, so the state constraint is the primary ground; its verbatim field is quoted. violates-declaration self-check applied honestly: the observed behavior does not contradict the quote — all 7 ops were applied in order (payload {"s":true} exact, 902 deleted, count 1) and each reported its own result; the update_vectors op demonstrably applied (readback direction == V2's). The E1 expectation that the readback vector must equal the RAW V2 byte-for-byte is OUTSIDE the claim domain of both constraints (neither pins vector-fidelity-on-readback) — this is the wrong-citation branch of the self-check: the oracle's guarantee has no constraint clause behind it. Co-anchor qdrant_behavioral_points_batch_001 expected_behavior (verbatim): 'batch update returns HTTP 200 with one result entry per operation; missing collection returns 404' — also satisfied by the observed 200/7-entries response.

chain_trace.break_detail: The E1 oracle demands GET readback vector == raw uploaded V2 in a Cosine-metric collection; no contract clause and no documentation link provides that guarantee (both constraints' claims — sequential application + one completed result entry per op — were observed honored). The verdict DEFECT_FOUND therefore rests on a script-invented requirement, not on the contract chain; the observed mismatch is fully explained by metric-level normalization (see source_grounding).

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST POST /collections/{name}/points/batch operations[].update_vectors -> VectorOperations::UpdateVectors (lib/collection/src/operations/vector_ops.rs:38, split_by_shard -> shards) -> SegmentEntry::update_vectors (lib/segment/src/segment/entry.rs:676) -> vectors.preprocess (entry.rs:684) -> NamedVectorStruct::preprocess_dense_vector (named_vectors.rs:335) -> Distance::preprocess_vector (types.rs:329) -> CosineMetric::preprocess (spaces/simple.rs:178) -> cosine_preprocess (simple.rs:228: x /= sqrt(sum(x^2))) -> NORMALIZED vector persisted -> GET point returns the stored normalized vector. Validation IS present (check_named_vectors dims check at entry.rs:683) — what is absent is any promise to store the RAW vector; normalization is applied identically on the upsert path (entry.rs:662) and hence on both REST faces (batch and PUT /points/vectors), exactly matching the live comparative probe (Cosine->normalized, Euclid->byte-exact, both faces).
source_grounding.by_design_evidence_note: Explicit intent evidence per tightened v3.4 rule: spaces/simple.rs:168 doc comment '/// Equivalent to DotProductMetric with normalization of the vectors in preprocessing.' declares the normalization design; cosine_preprocess skips only when is_length_zero_or_normalized (already-unit vectors pass through, e.g. the script's [0.5,0.75,1.0]-style unit seeds would read back unchanged); the same preprocess call sits on every write path. This is NOT an unannotated silent behavior.
